questions.q: In the table/row analogy, what does a field correspond to?
options: A column on an object, where every record has its own value or blank
questions.explain: A field is one column on an object; each record (row) has its own value — or no value — in that column.

questions.q: What is the three-click path to creating any new custom field?
options: Object Manager → the object → Fields & Relationships → New
questions.explain: Every custom field starts the same way: Object Manager, into the object, into Fields & Relationships, then New.

questions.q: What is the title of the first screen the New Custom Field wizard shows?
questions.explain: The wizard's first screen is titled "Step 1. Choose the field type," grouping Data Type options into families.

questions.q: Why does this lesson stress getting a field's data type right on Step 1?
options: Because the data type can be freely changed at any time with no consequences
Because the data type is largely locked in once saved — only narrow conversions are allowed later
Because the data type only affects the field's color
Because Step 1 has no effect on the field at all
questions.explain: A field's data type is mostly fixed after creation; Salesforce allows only a few narrow conversions (like Text to Picklist), not a full type change.

questions.q: Which two families does this lesson group "Lookup Relationship" and "Roll-Up Summary" into, respectively?
questions.explain: Lookup Relationship belongs to the relationship family (it connects two objects); Roll-Up Summary belongs to the calculated family (it computes a value).
